```{r Differential-Gene-expression}
## The differential expression analysis contains the following steps:
###### Import count data
###### Import data to DEseq2
###### Differential gene expression
###### QC plots
####### 1. Create a matrix containing the sample IDs. The matrix should have at least three columns: the first with the sample IDs, the second with the path to the salmon quant.sf files, and the third with the group (e.g. treatment or sample). This can be generated in excel, for example, and saved as a tab-delimited txt file called speccies.abb.tx.txt
####### 2. Create transcript to gene ID file
samplet0015 <- read.table("~/Desktop/EvoPhosphoOmics/metadata/Calb/Calb.t0015.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
samplet0015$group <- factor(samplet0015$group)  # ensure group is a factor

# Set named vector of quant.sf file paths
files <- setNames(as.character(samplet0015$path), samplet0015$id)

# Make sure you're in the right directory or use full path
txdb <- makeTxDbFromGFF("refs/SC5314Ca.gtf", format = "gtf")

tx2gene <- select(txdb, keys(txdb, "TXNAME"), "GENEID", "TXNAME")
#dir.create("analysis", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.table(tx2gene, file = "metadata/Calb.tx2gene.txt", quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE)

##### 3 Read in the transcript to gene ID file
#Read tx2gene mapping
tx2gene <- read.table("~/Desktop/EvoPhosphoOmics/metadata/Calb/Calb.tx2gene.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")

##### 4 Read in the count data using tximport. This will combine the transcript-level counts to gene-level.
# Run tximport
txi <- tximport(files, type = "salmon", tx2gene = tx2gene)


##### 5. Import data to DEseq2.
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromTximport(txi,
                                colData = samplet0015,
                                design = ~ group)
## run DESeq2 
ddst0015 <- DESeq(dds)

## Extract raw counts 
rawt0015_counts <- counts(ddst0015, normalized = FALSE)  # same as tximport's estimatedCounts

#####  Extract normalized counts (by DESeq2
normt0015_counts <- counts(ddst0015, normalized = TRUE)



#### 6 Stabilizing DESeq estimates for downstream visualization.There are several models available to calculate differential gene expression. Here, the apeglm (Approximate Posterior Estimation for Generalized Linear Models) shrinkage method will be applied to shrink high log-fold changes with little statistical evidence and account for lowly expressed genes with significant deviation

# resultsNames(ddst0015)
LFCt0015shrink <- lfcShrink(ddst0015, coef = "group_Treatment_vs_Control", type = "apeglm")

##### 7 QC plots. Before moving on to functional analysis, such as gene set enrichment analysis, quality control should be carried out on the differential expression analyses. The types of plots which will be generated below are:
###### Principal component analysis - sample clustering
###### Biological replicate correlation
###### MA plot
###### p-value distribution
###### Volcano plot
######### I. Principal component analysis. A common component of analysing RNA-seq data is to carry out QC by testing if expected samples cluster together. One popular tool is principal component analysis (PCA)

rldt0015 <- rlog(ddst0015, blind = TRUE)##regularized log transformation.Blind Ignores experimental design.
rld_mat0015 <- assay(rldt0015)##Extracts the normalized expression matrix from
pcat0015 <- prcomp(t(rld_mat0015))## Run PCA to assess clustering of

#### pca$x: coordinates of your samples (principal components)
#### pca$sdev: standard deviations (to calculate % variance explained)
#### pca$rotation: loadings (genes’ contributions)

p <- ggplot(df_out0015, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = group, label = sample)) +
  geom_point(size = 6, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(vjust = -1.5, size = 6, fontface = "bold") +  # Bold & larger text labels
  labs(
    title = "No batch effect removed",
    x = xlab,
    y = ylab,
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 22, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.key.size = unit(1, "cm")
  ) +
  xlim(-25, 25) +
  ylim(-7, 7)

p


### II Distribution of p-values and FDRs. The distribution of p-values following a differential expression analysis can be an indication of whether there is an enrichment of differentially expressed genes and whether the statistical test is correct, i.e. has the correct assumptions.
#The distribution of p-values
# Plot histogram of raw p-values
p_dist <- hist(LFCt0015shrink$pvalue,
     breaks = 50,
     col = "grey",
     main = "Distribution of Raw p-values",
     xlab = "p-values",
     ylab = "Frequency",
     cex.main = 1.5,
     cex.lab = 1.2,
     cex.axis = 1)

# Plot histogram of adjusted p-values (FDR)
p_FDR <- hist(LFCt0015shrink$padj,
     breaks = 50,
     col = "grey",
     main = "Distribution of Adjusted p-values (FDR)",
     xlab = "FDR",
     ylab = "Frequency",
     cex.main = 1.5,
     cex.lab = 1.2,
     cex.axis = 1)

p_dist
p_FDR 

#### III An MA plot is a scatter plot of the log fold-change between two samples against the average gene expression (mean of normalised counts). An MA plot can be generated using the following command from DEseq2:
#Add a title to reflect your comparison 
p_MA <- plotMA(LFCt0015shrink, main = 'Calb t0015', cex = 0.5)

p_MA

### IV.A volcano plot is a scatterplot which plots the p-value of differential expression against the fold-change. The volcano plot can be designed to highlight datapoints of significant genes, with a p-value and fold-change cut off.

#Allow for more space around the borders of the plot
par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 4))

#Set your log-fold-change and p-value thresholds
lfc = 2
pval = 0.05

tab = data.frame(logFC = LFCt0015shrink$log2FoldChange, negLogPval = -log10(LFCt0015shrink$padj))#make a data frame with the log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values

plot(tab, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, xlab = expression(bold(log[2]~fold~change)),
     ylab = expression(bold(-log[10]~pvalue)), main = 'Calb t0015') #replace main = with your title

#Genes with a fold-change greater than 2 and p-value<0.05:
signGenes = (abs(tab$logFC) > lfc & tab$negLogPval > -log10(pval))

#Colour these red
points(tab[signGenes, ], pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = "red")

#Show the cut-off lines
abline(h = -log10(pval), col = "green3", lty = 2)
abline(v = c(-lfc, lfc), col = "blue", lty = 2)

# Annotations for thresholds
mtext(paste("FDR =", pval), side = 4, at = -log10(pval),
      cex = 1, font = 2, line = 0.5, las = 1)
mtext(c(paste("-", lfc, "fold"), paste("+", lfc, "fold")), side = 3,
      at = c(-lfc, lfc), cex = 1, font = 2, line = 0.5)

### Data exploration
######## How many genes are differentially expressed? What are the top DEGs? How do I plot the expression for candidate genes?
######## 1. How many genes are differentially expressed?
#increased expression
attach(as.data.frame(LFCt0015shrink))

#The total number of DEGs with an adjusted p-value<0.05
summary(LFCt0015shrink, alpha=0.05)

#The total number of DEGs with an adjusted p-value<0.05 AND absolute fold-change > 2
sum(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >2)

#Decreased expression:
anylfclessthanzero <- sum(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange <0) #any fold-change
lfcgrt2 <- sum(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange <(-2)) #fold-change greater than 2

#Increased expression:
anylfcgrtzero <- sum(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange >0) #any fold-change
lfcgrt2 <- sum(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange >2) #fold-change greater than 2

anylfclessthanzero 
lfcgrt2
anylfcgrtzero 
lfcgrt2


#### What are the top genes?
LFC.t0015.gene <- as.data.frame(LFCt0015)

### Keep only significant genes
LFC.t0015.sig <- LFC.t0015.gene[which(!is.na(LFC.t0015.gene$padj) & LFC.t0015.gene$padj < 0.05), ]

# Convert rownames to a column for merging
LFC.t0015.sig$GeneID <- rownames(LFC.t0015.sig)

# Join annotation
LFC.t0015.sig.annotated <- LFC.t0015.sig %>%
  left_join(CalbSC5314.annot, by = "GeneID")

#### Count how many are missing
sum(is.na(LFC.t0015.sig.annotated$Chr))

####### View genes without annotation

LFC.t0015.sig.annotated %>%
  filter(is.na(Chr)) %>%
  select(GeneID, log2FoldChange, padj)

#####  Top 10 by adjusted p-value (padj)
Calb.t0015.top10.genes <- LFC.t0015.sig.annotated %>%
  arrange(padj) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

# View the result
Calb.t0015.top10.genes %>%
  select(GeneID, GeneName, log2FoldChange, padj, FungiDB_ID)

# Define top 10 genes
Calb.t0015.top10.ids <- c("orf19.1030", "orf19.1047", "orf19.1065", "orf19.1199", "orf19.1566",
                          "orf19.1631", "orf19.1633", "orf19.1646", "orf19.1687", "orf19.1691")

# Theme setup
my_theme <- theme(panel.background = element_blank(),
                  panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA),
                  plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
                  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Loop through genes and plot
for (gene_id in Calb.t0015.top10.ids) {
  
  matched_gene <- grep(gene_id, rownames(ddst0015), value = TRUE)
  
  if (length(matched_gene) == 0) {
    message("Gene not found: ", gene_id)
    next
  }
  
  tmp <- plotCounts(ddst0015, gene = matched_gene, intgroup = "group", returnData = TRUE)
  
  p_top10 <- ggplot(tmp, aes(x = group, y = count)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_dotplot(binaxis = 'y', stackdir = 'center', dotsize = 0.6) +
    ggtitle(paste(gene_id, " expression")) +
    ylab("Normalized count") +
    my_theme
  
  print(p_top10)
}

```

```{r Calb-15min-DESeq, echo=FALSE}
########  Chris count matrix 
# Load count matrix
ca_counts <- read.delim("~/Desktop/EvoPhosphoOmics/metadata/counts_Hubert/Ca.salmon.merged.gene_counts.tsv", row.names = 1)

# Automatically select all t0000 and t0015 replicates
selected_cols <- grep("t0000|t0015", colnames(ca_counts), value = TRUE)
ca_counts_15min <- ca_counts[, selected_cols]
ca_counts_15min <- as.data.frame(lapply(ca_counts_15min, as.integer))
rownames(ca_counts_15min) <- rownames(ca_counts)


# Define sample metadata based on column names
conditions <- ifelse(grepl("t0000", selected_cols), "untreated", "treated")
ca_coldata <- data.frame(
  row.names = selected_cols,
  condition = factor(conditions, levels = c("untreated", "treated"))
)

# Create DESeq2 object
ca_dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = ca_counts_15min,
  colData = ca_coldata,
  design = ~ condition
)

# Run DESeq2 and shrink fold changes
ca_dds <- DESeq(ca_dds)
ca_res <- results(ca_dds)
#resultsNames(ca_dds)
caLFCshrink <- lfcShrink(ca_dds, coef = "condition_treated_vs_untreated", type = "apeglm")

# Rlog transformation
rld_ca <- rlog(ca_dds, blind = TRUE)
rld_mat_ca <- assay(rld_ca)

# PCA
pca_ca <- prcomp(t(rld_mat_ca))
percentVar <- round(100 * (pca_ca$sdev^2 / sum(pca_ca$sdev^2)))

# PCA metadata
Casample_info <- as.data.frame(colData(ca_dds))
Casample_info$sample <- rownames(Casample_info)

df_pca <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca_ca$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca_ca$x[, 2],
  sample = rownames(pca_ca$x),
  group = Casample_info$condition
)

# PCA plot
CaPCA1 <- ggplot(df_pca, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 6, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA - Calb 15 mins",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", percentVar[1], "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", percentVar[2], "%)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 22, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.key.size = unit(1, "cm")
  ) +

# Load count matrix
ca_counts2 <- read.csv("~/Desktop/EvoPhosphoOmics/metadata/Calb/20250714Calb_Rawcounts.csv")

# Set GeneID as rownames
rownames(ca_counts2) <- make.unique(as.character(ca_counts2$GeneID))

# Subset only the actual count columns (5th onward)
ca_counts2 <- ca_counts2[, grep("^Calb\\.t.*\\.rep\\d$", colnames(ca_counts2))]

# Subset 0min and 15min timepoints
ca_15min_counts2 <- ca_counts2[, c("Calb.t0000.rep1", "Calb.t0000.rep2",
                                  "Calb.t0015.rep1", "Calb.t0015.rep2")]

# Create colData
ca_15min_coldata <- data.frame(
  row.names = colnames(ca_15min_counts2),
  condition = factor(c("untreated", "untreated", "treated", "treated"))
)

# Construct DESeqDataSet
ca_15min_dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = ca_15min_counts,
  colData = ca_15min_coldata,
  design = ~ condition
)

# Run DESeq
ca_15min_dds <- DESeq(ca_15min_dds)
ca_15min_res <- results(ca_15min_dds)

# Shrink LFCs
ca_15min_LFCshrink <- lfcShrink(ca_15min_dds,
                                coef = "condition_untreated_vs_treated",
                                type = "apeglm")

# Rlog transform
rld_ca15 <- rlog(ca_15min_dds, blind = TRUE)
rld_mat_ca15 <- assay(rld_ca15)

# PCA

percentVar <- round(100 * (pca_ca15$sdev^2 / sum(pca_ca15$sdev^2)))

sample_info_ca15 <- as.data.frame(colData(ca_15min_dds))
sample_info_ca15$sample <- rownames(sample_info_ca15)

df_pca_ca15 <- data.frame(

  PC2 = pca_ca15$x[, 2],
  sample = rownames(pca_ca15$x),
  group = sample_info_ca15$condition
)

# PCA plot

  geom_point(size = 6, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(vjust = -1.5, size = 6, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = "PCA - Calb 15min",
    x = paste0("PC1 (", percentVar[1], "%)"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", percentVar[2], "%)")

# Ensure rownames are characters (not factors)

rownames(ca_15min_counts2) <- as.character(rownames(ca_15min_counts2))

# Subset both matrices to only include shared genes

ca_15min_2 <- ca_15min_counts2[common_genes, ]

# Combine them side-by-side
ca_combined <- cbind(ca_15min_1, ca_15min_2)

# Correlation of total counts per gene
gene_corr <- cor(rowSums(ca_15min_1), rowSums(ca_15min_2), method = "pearson")
cat("Gene-wise Pearson correlation of total counts:", gene_corr, "\n")

)

##### Paired t-test on Log Counts Test if the means of log counts are significantly different across matched samples:
# Untreated group: b1 and b4 biological replicates
ca_t0000_b1 <- rowSums(ca_counts_15min[, c("Calb.t0000.b1.L001", "Calb.t0000.b1.L002")])
ca_t0000_b4 <- rowSums(ca_counts_15min[, c("Calb.t0000.b4.L001", "Calb.t0000.b4.L002")])

# Treated group: b1 and b2 biological replicates
ca_t0015_b1 <- rowSums(ca_counts_15min[, c("Calb.t0015.b1.L001", "Calb.t0015.b1.L002")])
ca_t0015_b2 <- rowSums(ca_counts_15min[, c("Calb.t0015.b2.L001", "Calb.t0015.b2.L002")])
ca_collapsed <- data.frame(
  Calb.t0000.b1 = ca_t0000_b1,
  Calb.t0000.b4 = ca_t0000_b4,
  Calb.t0015.b1 = ca_t0015_b1,
  Calb.t0015.b2 = ca_t0015_b2
)

common_genes <- intersect(rownames(ca_collapsed), rownames(ca_15min_counts2))
ca_collapsed <- ca_collapsed[common_genes, ]
ca_reference <- ca_15min_counts2[common_genes, ]

log_collapsed <- log2(ca_collapsed + 1)
log_reference <- log2(ca_reference + 1)

t.test(rowMeans(log_collapsed), rowMeans(log_reference), paired = TRUE)

####################
#### Assess agreement between two sets of measurements:
means <- rowMeans(log_collapsed  + log_reference) / 2
diffs <- rowMeans(log_collapsed) - rowMeans(log_reference)

plot(means, diffs, pch = 16, col = "darkgreen",
     main = "Bland-Altman Plot", xlab = "Mean log2(counts)", ylab = "Difference")
abline(h = mean(diffs), col = "red")
abline(h = mean(diffs) + 2*sd(diffs), lty = 2)
abline(h = mean(diffs) - 2*sd(diffs), lty = 2)


################
################ Bland-Altman Plot
plot(rowMeans(log_collapsed), rowMeans(log_reference),
     xlab = "nfc core collapsed log2 counts",
     ylab = "josh log2 counts",
     main = "nfc core counts vs josh counts",
     col = "blue", pch = 16)
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
cor(rowMeans(log_collapsed), rowMeans(log_reference), method = "pearson")
###########################
top_genes <- head(order(apply(abs(log_collapsed - log_reference), 1, sd), decreasing = TRUE), 50)
pheatmap(log_collapsed[top_genes, ] - log_reference[top_genes, ])
#########################
hist(rowMeans(log_collapsed) - rowMeans(log_reference),
     breaks = 50, col = "grey",
     main = "Histogram of Log2 Differences",
     xlab = "log2(collapsed) - log2(reference)")
```
